title: A protocol for ultra-high field laminar fMRI in the human brain
author: Jia, Zamboni, et al.
materials: Use AFNI or FSL TOPUP for distortion correction.
This protocol did not generate any unique reagents.

steps.title: Participant screening
steps.instruction: Complete all pre‑scan paperwork and practice the task the day before scanning (≈1 h total).

substeps.instruction: Complete safety screening form (~10 min).
Sign consent form (~5 min).
Introduce experiment, give instructions, and practice task (~5 min intro + 5 min instructions + 20 min practice).
Fill personal information sheet (age, medication, visual acuity, etc.) (~10 min).

steps.title: Scan setup and participant preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the scanner console, stimulus computer, and participant for a 7 T scan (≈30 min).

substeps.instruction: Turn on stimulus computer; set resolution and frame rate as required by the experimental design.
Verify scanner triggers and button‑box responses are registered by the stimulus computer.
Position projection screen at the correct viewing distance.
Ask participant to change into MR‑compatible scrubs, remove all non‑MR items, and lie comfortably on the table.
Provide earplugs, pillows, immobilisation cushions, respiratory belt, and pulse oximeter; instruct participant not to cross limbs and to squeeze the safety ball if uncomfortable.
Move the table slowly into the bore; stop if dizziness occurs, allow recovery, then continue.
Instruct participant to stay as still as possible; use yes/no questions on screen for communication; prohibit talking unless necessary.
Fit earplugs correctly (≈37 dB attenuation) and verify proper fit before scanning.
Adjust mirror system so the participant can see the full stimulus screen; if visibility is insufficient, modify stimulus presentation scripts.

steps.title: Participant registration
steps.instruction: Register the participant according to local procedures before scanning.

steps.title: Localizer scan
steps.instruction: Run a localizer scan at isocentre to obtain a basic brain localisation.

steps.title: B1 mapping and transmit calibration
steps.instruction: Acquire a whole‑brain B1 map aligned to AC‑PC, load the flip‑angle map in Syngo, and set the transmit reference amplitude.

substeps.instruction: Draw an ROI on the sagittal image using the circle ROI tool.
Calculate (900 × Transmit Reference Amplitude) / Mean average; ensure the result ≤ 300 V (if higher, cap at 300 V).

steps.title: Acquire anatomical MP2RAGE
steps.instruction: Collect high‑resolution T1‑weighted MP2RAGE images (TR = 5000 ms, TE = 2.56 ms, FOV = 208 × 208 mm², 0.65 mm isotropic, 240 sagittal slices).

steps.title: Position functional fMRI slab
steps.instruction: Set up a 2D GE‑EPI slab covering the region of interest with the specified parameters.

substeps.instruction: Parameters: TR = 2060 ms, TE = 26.4 ms, FOV = 148 × 148 mm², flip angle = 70°, 0.8 mm isotropic resolution, 56 slices, partial Fourier = 6/8, GRAPPA = 3, MB factor = 2, bandwidth = 1034 Hz/px, echo spacing = 1.09 ms.
Confirm the area of interest is fully contained within the slab.
Check phase‑encoding direction.
Scroll through slices to verify full coverage.
Ensure no wrap‑around, ghosting, or signal drop‑outs.

steps.title: Check slab position
steps.instruction: Run a single volume of the slab to verify the field‑of‑view placement.

steps.title: Iterate slab positioning
steps.instruction: If the slab position is poor, repeat the positioning (step 7) and re‑check (step 8) until coverage is satisfactory.

steps.title: Shim volume adjustment and B0 shimming
steps.instruction: Adjust the shim volume and perform B0 shimming to achieve a water‑spectrum FWHM of ~30 Hz.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mm in all directions to the shim volume.
In Syngo: Options > Adjustments > Transmitter → enter the B1‑mapping amplitude value; Apply.
Manual shimming: Options > Adjustments > Frequency tab → click Go until convergence; Apply.
Repeat three times: Options > 3D Shim tab → Measure, Calculate, Apply.
Inter‑Shim tab: adjust Z, Y, X, Z2 currents to reduce water FWHM to ~30 Hz; Stop then Apply.

steps.title: Measure B0 map
steps.instruction: Acquire a whole‑brain B0 map using the same geometry as the functional slab.

substeps.instruction: Copy adjustment volume and centre of slices from the fMRI slab (step 7).
Move slices to obtain full brain coverage and run the B0 map scan.

steps.title: Acquire inverted PE scan
steps.instruction: Collect a short (5‑volume) EPI scan with opposite phase‑encoding direction for distortion correction.

substeps.instruction: Copy adjustment volume from the B0 map.
Copy centre of slices and phase‑encoding direction from the functional slab.
Set phase‑encoding direction to FH (foot‑to‑head) and number of measurements to 5; run scan.

steps.title: Acquire experimental functional data
steps.instruction: Collect the main functional runs with the intended phase‑encoding direction.

substeps.instruction: Copy adjustment volume from the B0 map.
Copy centre of slices and phase‑encoding direction from the functional slab.
Set phase‑encoding direction to HF (head‑to‑foot) and set the number of measurements according to the experimental design; run scan.

steps.title: Pair inverted and experimental scans
steps.instruction: Run the inverted‑PE scan (step 12) immediately before each experimental run (step 13) to minimise between‑run head motion and enable distortion correction.

substeps.instruction: After each pair, visually inspect the data for ghosting or signal drop‑outs.

steps.title: Repeat runs for all conditions
steps.instruction: Repeat the paired scans (steps 12–13) for every experimental run, keeping the participant as still as possible.

steps.title: Save raw imaging data
steps.instruction: Store all acquired anatomical, B0, inverted‑PE, and functional datasets.

steps.title: Convert DICOM to NIfTI
steps.instruction: Transform raw DICOM files to NIfTI format using SPM.

substeps.instruction: In MATLAB, launch SPM, choose DICOM Import, select files, set output directory, and click GO.

steps.title: FreeSurfer segmentation
steps.instruction: Run FreeSurfer recon‑all with high‑resolution settings to obtain WM‑GM segmentation and cortical surfaces.

substeps.instruction: Set environment variables: export FREESURFER_HOME=/Your/Path/to/FreeSurfer; source $FREESURFER_HOME/SetUpFreeSurfer.sh; export SUBJECT_DIR=/Your/Path/to/FreeSurfer/YourFolder.
Create expert.opt with mris_inflate = 100.
Execute: recon-all –all –s OUTPUTFOLDERNAME –hires –i INPUTFILE.nii –expert expert.opt.
Inspect results in freeview.

Convert outputs to NIfTI: mri_label2vol –seg ribbon.mgz –temp rawavg.mgz –o ribbon-in-rawavg.mgz –regheader ribbon.mgz; mri_convert ribbon-in-rawavg.mgz ribbon-in-rawavg.nii; mri_convert rawavg.mgz rawavg.nii.

steps.title: Manual ITK‑SNAP refinement
steps.instruction: Manually edit the WM‑GM segmentation in ITK‑SNAP for improved accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Assign a name, integer label, and colour to each tissue class; save label set for later reuse.
Define foreground (painted) and background labels to avoid overlapping assignments.
Select Paintbrush tool, choose label, set brush size/style, draw (left click) or erase (right click). Toggle segmentation view with S, change transparency with A, opacity with D.
Assess quality: open 3D rendering window, click UPDATE, rotate to inspect; examine 2D slice boundaries for consistency.
Save the refined segmentation as scanID_ribbon_fixed.nii.

steps.title: Generate meshes and inflate surfaces
steps.instruction: Create cortical meshes for each hemisphere and inflate them using BrainVoyager.

substeps.instruction: Load scanID_ribbon_fixed.nii in BrainVoyager; save as a VMR.
For left hemisphere: save copy as scanID_segmentation_LH.vmr; set intensity values – GM = 100, WM = 150.

Load secondary VMR if needed; ensure only LH GM/WM selected; delete unnecessary voxels; set WM‑only mask values (Min = 0, Max = 149 → New = 0; Min = 150, Max = 150 → New = 240). Save as scanID_segmentation_LH_WM_mask.f.
Advanced Mesh Smoothing (no shrinking).
Calculate curvature, smooth, and save as scanID_segmentation_LH_curvature_smoothed.
Inflate mesh: Meshes → Mesh Morphing; set reference to created mesh; Iterations = 1000; GO; save as scanID_curvature_smoothed_inflated.
Repeat the entire procedure for the right hemisphere.

steps.title: Create cortical depth layers
steps.instruction: Generate three cortical depth layers (superficial, middle, deep) in BrainVoyager.

substeps.instruction: Load the segmentation VMR; choose Volumes → Cortical Thickness Measurement → GO (produces scanID_segmentation_Thickness.vmp).
Mid‑GM Volume Tab → Create Volume → Create VOI (produces scanID_segmentation_Mid‑GM.vmr).
Under 3D Tools → Segmentation, click Prep and Reco; generate mesh, apply Advanced Smoothing; save as CorticalDepth_smoothed in VMR folder.
Load scanID_segmentation.vmr and the mesh from the previous step.
Meshes → Cortical Depth Sampling: select scanID_segmentation_Thickness file; Save Meshes as VOIs (default 4 meshes); GO.
Three layers appear; save them together as wholeBrain_layers.voi.

steps.title: Functional data quality check
steps.instruction: Visually and quantitatively assess each functional run for motion, signal, and distortion artifacts.

substeps.instruction: Load each run FMR; Options → Time Course Movie to view head motion; note volumes with large jumps.
Select an ROI in a slice; view its time‑course to detect drifts, drop‑outs, or spikes.
Load the inverse‑PE (IPE) scan FMR; toggle between EPI and IPE to evaluate geometric distortions.
Run the mcheck Matlab toolbox on the FMRs; verify correlation values are within 0.9–1.

steps.title: Distortion correction with COPE
steps.instruction: Correct EPI distortions using the COPE plugin in BrainVoyager.

substeps.instruction: Confirm COPE plugin is installed.
For each run, select the SBRef images for IPE and EPI; estimate a voxel displacement map (VDM).
Undistort data: Undistort Data (Apply VDM) tab → select SBRef and MultiBand EPI images of the run → Apply VDM.
Load the resulting scanID_undist.fmr files (IPE and EPI) and verify that distortions are reduced.

steps.title: Slice‑time, filtering, and motion correction
steps.instruction: Perform slice‑time correction, temporal filtering, and 3D motion correction on each undistorted functional run.

substeps.instruction: Load undistorted FMR; Analysis → FMR Data Preprocessing; keep default options.
Advanced → 3D Motion Options: select “Use other FMR for intra‑session alignment”, choose the SBRef of the first EPI run; OK; GO.
Inspect motion‑corrected output; run checkMotion.m from the mcheck toolbox; mean correlation should exceed 0.9.
Convert corrected FMR to identical VTC/VDW via Options → Convert FMR/DMR to Identical VTC/VDW.
Note: slice‑time correction may be omitted for block designs; order of distortion and motion correction can be swapped if needed.

steps.title: Coregister functional to anatomical data
steps.instruction: Align functional volumes to the anatomical VMR using initial alignment and boundary‑based registration (BBR).

substeps.instruction: Initial alignment: open FMR‑VMR Coregistration dialog; run header‑based IA; select SBRef of first run; check “Save VMR for BBR”. This creates a VMR named *_IA_For‑BBR.vmr.

Generate cortex mesh for BBR: load manually refined segmentation VMR; create WM‑only mask (value ranges Min = 0, Max = 149 → New = 0; Min = 150, Max = 150 → New = 240); apply Gaussian filtering; set final WM mask values (Min = 0, Max = 0 → New = 0; Min = 100, Max = 225 → New = 240); save as scanID_segmentation_WM_mask; run Prep and Reco; Advanced Mesh Smoothing (no shrinking); calculate curvature, smooth; save as scanID_segmentation_forBBR_smoothed_curvature.fmr.
Fine‑tuning BBR: load the functional VMR (from SBRef) and the cortex mesh; Meshes → Boundary‑Based Registration; GO; produces a fine‑tuning transformation (FA) matrix.

steps.title: Transform ROIs into functional space
steps.instruction: Apply the IA and FA transformations to bring anatomical ROIs into functional space.

substeps.instruction: Open the anatomical VMR; Options → Transform Native VMR to FMR‑VTC Space; select IA, FA, and the functional FMR files generated in steps 24a‑c; GO. This creates an anatomical file in functional space and a transformation matrix.
Open the anatomical VMR again; load the ROI defined in anatomical space; Options → Transformations tab; select the matrix from the previous substep; Apply. The ROI is now saved in functional space.

steps.title: Correct superficial vascular bias
steps.instruction: Identify and remove vein‑related voxels and regress out superficial‑layer contamination.

substeps.instruction: Exclude vein voxels:
Compute temporal SNR (tSNR) for each voxel in the ROI; flag low‑tSNR voxels that appear dark on T2* images.
Run a GLM (stimulus vs fixation) per voxel; compute t‑scores.
Exclude voxels with low tSNR or with t‑scores above the 90th percentile.
Spatial regression:
For each superficial‑layer voxel, find the nearest middle‑layer voxel.
Regress the mean time‑course of the middle‑layer voxels from the superficial‑layer voxel time‑courses.
Save the residual time‑courses for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Save processed datasets
steps.instruction: Store all final anatomical, functional, mesh, layer, and ROI files for further analysis.
